Title: Approved security policy set is absent
Criteria: A formalized and approved information security policy suite must define corporate asset protection rules, explicit personnel responsibilities, and mandatory annual review dates.
Condition: No approved information security policy documentation or history of executive management review was provided for evaluation under EV-001.
Cause: Security governance has historically been treated as an ad-hoc operational task without structured programmatic requirements or formal executive validation.
Risk: The absence of clear security policies leads to inconsistent access controls, uncoordinated baseline configurations, and increased operational vulnerability to identity theft or service outages.
Recommendation: Draft, approve, and distribute core security policies addressing identity governance, asset protection, and incident response requirements.
Validation_Step: Approved policies explicitly show assigned owners, required annual review dates, and formal exception logs.

Title: Risk baseline lacks approval and recurring review
Criteria: Cybersecurity risk parameters must be consistently assessed, mathematically validated, officially signed off by management, and monitored on a recurring basis.
Condition: A baseline risk assessment exists under EV-003, but official executive management approval records and recurring review schedules are not currently evidenced.
Cause: The risk assessment framework was recently introduced as part of the initial compliance program and has not yet been integrated into standard governance workflows.
Risk: Unapproved risk assumptions can result in a misallocation of security budgets, leaving critical operational vulnerabilities unmitigated or untracked by the executive suite.
Recommendation: Submit the baseline risk register to leadership for formal sign-off and schedule a recurring monthly review session to track active remediations.
Validation_Step: Management approval is formally archived and a recurring monthly risk review session is scheduled on the corporate calendar.

Title: MFA is not enforced for all workforce identities
Criteria: Multi-factor authentication must be centrally enforced for 100% of active workforce and administrative identities, and legacy authentication channels must be explicitly blocked.
Condition: Configuration summary EV-004 indicates that MFA is active for only 4 administrator accounts out of 60 active workforce identities, leaving a 93.3 percentage-point gap. Legacy authentication blocking is unevidenced.
Cause: Conditional access rules have historically been restricted to high-privilege administrators to minimize friction for general business users.
Risk: Threat actors can exploit standard user accounts via phishing or credential stuffing, using compromised mailboxes to conduct business email compromise or lateral movement.
Recommendation: Configure and enforce a tenant-wide conditional access policy mandating MFA for all user sign-ins and explicitly disable legacy authentication.
Validation_Step: A sanitized configuration export demonstrates 100% active workforce identity coverage and legacy authentication is blocked.

Title: Quarterly access review is not established
Criteria: A formal access entitlement review must be performed quarterly to validate active, privileged, dormant, and departed accounts across all core corporate systems.
Condition: No documentation or operational records of regular user access reviews or employee offboarding verification logs were available under EV-005.
Cause: User account lifecycle management relies entirely on manual offboarding notifications without a structured verification or reconciliation schedule.
Risk: Dormant accounts or over-privileged former employees could retain active permissions, leading to unauthorized sensitive data access or insider threat incidents.
Recommendation: Establish a mandatory quarterly access review procedure and construct an integrated joiner-mover-leaver validation checklist.
Validation_Step: The initial completed quarterly access review is archived, confirming verification across active, privileged, dormant, and departed accounts.

Title: Critical patching lacks an approved target and evidence
Criteria: Critical vulnerabilities and software operating system patches must be identified and remediated within strict, documented timeframes (such as 14 days for critical exposure).
Condition: Vulnerability management under EV-006 relies on informal administrative notes; there are no approved SLAs, tracking reports, or automated scanning verifications.
Cause: Systems maintenance tasks are executed reactively rather than via structured vulnerability scanning cycles or formalized target windows.
Risk: Unpatched software vulnerabilities on internet-facing application layers provide an explicit entry point for automated exploits, leading to full server compromise.
Recommendation: Define a strict 14-day critical patch remediation target window, deploy automated vulnerability scanning tools, and generate compliance reports.
Validation_Step: An automated system patch report demonstrates zero overdue Critical vulnerabilities or contains approved exception logs.

Title: Secure configuration baselines are not approved
Criteria: Standardized system hardening baselines must be formally defined, approved, applied to all endpoints and servers, and audited for compliance deviations.
Condition: No documented security configuration standards or automated baseline compliance checks were provided for evaluation under EV-007.
Cause: Systems are deployed utilizing vendor-default out-of-the-box configurations to speed up initial infrastructure setups.
Risk: Default configurations often leave unnecessary services running and weaken local system defenses, facilitating lateral malware movement or unauthorized persistence.
Recommendation: Adopt industry-standard hardening benchmarks (such as CIS Benchmarks) for Windows endpoints and Ubuntu servers, and implement compliance auditing.
Validation_Step: Configuration audit reports show that selected Windows and Ubuntu systems satisfy the target baseline checks or possess approved deviations.

Title: High-risk CloudTrail review is not defined
Criteria: High-risk administrative cloud configuration changes must be automatically logged, routinely reviewed, and escalated when unauthorized anomalies are detected.
Condition: CloudTrail logging is active under EV-008, but priority event definitions, review frequencies, escalation procedures, and verification samples are absent.
Cause: Log collection pipelines were configured during initial cloud architecture deployment, but review workflows and continuous monitoring teams were not established.
Risk: Unauthorized structural changes to infrastructure configurations, network routing tables, or IAM permissions could go undetected for an extended period.
Recommendation: Draft a formal cloud log review procedure, define priority high-risk events, and configure daily monitoring alerts within the SIEM platform.
Validation_Step: A documented review procedure and a complete sample of consecutive daily reviews demonstrate successful anomaly tracking and escalation.

Title: Incident-response plan is unapproved and untested
Criteria: An incident response plan defining clear operational roles, severity categories, communication chains, and recurring tabletop simulations must be formally authorized.
Condition: The incident plan provided under EV-009 remains an unapproved draft; severity tiers are incomplete and no testing simulations have been run in the past 12 months.
Cause: The response plan has been treated as a static planning document rather than a continuously maintained, tested, and validated operational framework.
Risk: A disorganized response to a live cyber attack can severely delay containment boundaries, leading to extended service downtime, data loss, or regulatory penalties.
Recommendation: Formally approve the incident response plan, establish an internal triage matrix, and execute a multi-departmental ransomware tabletop simulation.
Validation_Step: An officially approved corporate incident plan is archived alongside the action logs from a completed ransomware tabletop simulation.

Title: Backup recoverability has not been demonstrated
Criteria: Critical backup data must be restored at least quarterly, validated for integrity, timed against the approved RTO, and followed by corrective action for failures.
Condition: Automated backup-job completion was simulated as available, but no restore execution, integrity result, elapsed recovery time, or exception record was provided.
Cause: Restore testing has no named schedule, owner checklist, or evidence-retention requirement.
Risk: During ransomware or destructive failure, backup data may be unusable or too slow to restore, interrupting checkout and customer services beyond the four-hour target.
Recommendation: Perform a controlled restore within 14 days, validate selected records, record elapsed time, document failures, and schedule quarterly retesting.
Validation_Step: Controlled restore completes, data integrity passes, time is recorded
